messages:
nisha: heads-up: new hire couldn't run sample-app in linux CI after we pushed wheels to our private index. works locally on mac, but CI can't install wheel due to platform tag mismatch + typing missing for async module.

nisha: logs: `redwood_client-0.8.1-cp310-cp310-manylinux_2_17_x86_64.manylinux_2_17_x86_64.whl is not a supported wheel on this platform` and mypy says `package is not typed` for redwood_client.aio

roland: oh man. what did our build pipeline produce? we use cibuildwheel on GHA to build manylinux and macos wheels and upload to artifactory. Which runner produced that wheel?

nisha: looks like the linux wheel was produced on an image that used musllinux / newer tag trickery, but the filename suggests manylinux_2_17 which should be fine for glibc upstream. CI runner is older (manylinux2014 compat) and pip refuses to accept the tag. I also see our mac osx wheel is fine.

ivy: two separate problems: 1) wheel platform tag / cibuildwheel matrix mismatch; 2) editable/dev install case where py.typed isn't present for the async subpackage. Are the packaging metadata entries for py.typed and package-data set?

nisha: pyproject has `include = ["redwood_client/py.typed"]` under tool.poetry. No setuptools fallback metadata. We also rely on cibuildwheel to create wheels. For editable installs (dev onboarding), the new hire used `poetry install --with dev` which created an editable-style install and mypy couldn't find py.typed for `redwood_client.aio`.

patrick: for the wheel mismatch: ensure cibuildwheel uses the correct `CIBW_MANYLINUX_X86_64_IMAGE` and `CIBW_MANYLINUX_I386_IMAGE` config and test on our CI images. We've had cases where local Docker images produce a wheel with a newer glibc tag than the target runtime. Quick fix: re-run builds on the official manylinux2014/manylinux_2_24 image, or use `cibuildwheel --platform linux --output-dir wheelhouse` in the proper container.

roland: agreed. Also check our `build` and `auditwheel` steps — auditwheel repair can rewrite tags incorrectly if run inside a newer chroot. We should pin cibuildwheel and auditwheel versions.

ivy: for the typing/editable issue: we should add a small `MANIFEST.in` with `include redwood_client/py.typed` and also add `tool.setuptools.package-data = {"redwood_client": ["py.typed"]}` to pyproject so non-poetry installers and PEP 660 backends see the metadata. That solved a similar case before.

nisha: quick repro I made: create new venv, `pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel`, then `poetry install --no-root --with dev` vs `poetry add --dev .` yield different outcomes. When poetry triggers PEP517 editable, pip ends up creating a .pth pointing to the source and some tools (mypy in our setup) only consult installed distribution metadata to find py.typed.

patrick: add a CI integration test: in packaging workflow, `python -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install -e .[dev] && venv/bin/python -c "import redwood_client.aio; print('ok')" && venv/bin/pytest -q`. Also add a small mypy check: `venv/bin/mypy -c "import redwood_client.aio"`. That will catch the editable drop.

roland: for the wheel tag problem, I added a CI job to rebuild the linux wheel using the pinned manylinux2014 image and reauditwheel. If the rebuilt wheel has manylinux2014 tag it works on our CI runner. I'll push that change and reupload to the private index.

nisha: thanks. I also opened a GitHub issue with reproduction steps for the editable-typing problem: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python/issues/512 (assigned to devex). Included matrix: poetry 1.5 vs 1.6, pip 23/24, mac arm vs manylinux2014 runner.

ivy: long-term we should: 1) make package metadata explicit (setuptools package-data), 2) add CI tests for editable installation + mypy, 3) document preferred dev loop (`pip install -e .[dev]` or wheel reinstall) in CONTRIBUTING.md, and 4) pin cibuildwheel/auditwheel and test manylinux images.

ci-bot: packaging test failed on manylinux-x86_64: tests/packaging/test_wheel_compat.py::test_manylinux_tag_mismatch (job https://ci.redwood/internal/4987)

patrick: I'll coordinate the re-build and a hotfix release (0.8.1.post1) containing the MANIFEST.in and package-data change. If the private index still refuses the wheel, we'll fall back to uploading a manylinux2014-compatible repair.

nisha: patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python/pull/542 adds MANIFEST.in, setuptools package-data entries, a new packaging CI job, and docs note about dev install caveats. Moving to review. Thanks y'all.
